issues.legal_issue: Income from taking property on lease, developing it, and subletting portions is business income when those activities form part of the taxpayer’s trading operations.
material_facts: The company’s objects included acquiring, improving, leasing, and commercially dealing with property.
Soon after incorporation, the company took a long-term lease of a market with the right to sublet portions.
The company undertook to remodel and repair the premises and developed them by letting shops, stalls, and ground spaces to vendors.
There was no finding that the company owned the property; it conducted the relevant activity as lessee.
issues.conclusion: The income from subletting was assessable as business income under section 10 of the Income-tax Act, 1922, rather than as income from other sources under section 12.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 2(4) and 10 of the Income-tax Act, 1922, business includes trading activity involving real property. The key consideration is whether acquiring and letting the property was an investment or instead an integral part of the taxpayer’s business and trading operations. The taxpayer’s objects and actual activities are relevant. The Court relied on Commissioner of Inland Revenue v. Korean Syndicate Ltd. and Karanpura Development Co. Ltd. v. Commissioner of Income-tax, and distinguished Fry v. Salisbury House Estate Ltd. and East India Housing and Land Development Trust Ltd. because those cases concerned income derived by an owner.

rule.if: income_tax_classification_case and taxpayer_is_lessee and commercial_property_object and subletting_was_operating_activity

predicates.income_tax_classification_case: The dispute concerns how receipts are to be classified for income-tax assessment.
predicates.taxpayer_is_lessee: The taxpayer acquired the property under a lease rather than as its owner.
predicates.commercial_property_object: The taxpayer’s stated objects included acquiring, improving, leasing, or commercially dealing with property.
predicates.subletting_was_operating_activity: The taxpayer developed the leased property and let portions of it as part of its commercial activity.
predicates.receipts_are_business_income: The receipts are classified as income from the taxpayer’s business activity.

issues.definition: When an income-tax classification case involves a lessee whose commercial property objects and operating activity include developing and subletting the property, the receipts are treated as business income.

issues.legal_issue: The residuary category for income from other sources applies only when the income does not fall within an earlier specific category, including business income.
material_facts: The company’s income arose from developing leased premises and subletting shops, stalls, and ground spaces.
The Tribunal found that taking the lease and subletting the premises were undertaken as business activity.
The Court held that the income appropriately fell within the business-income category.
issues.conclusion: Because the income was business income, it could not be assessed under section 12 of the Income-tax Act, 1922.
issues.legal_principle: Section 12(1) of the Income-tax Act, 1922, is a residuary provision and applies only to income not included under a preceding head. The Court held that it could be used only after the applicability of section 10 had been excluded.

predicates.income_tax_classification_case: The dispute concerns how receipts are to be classified for income-tax assessment.
predicates.income_arose_from_trading_operation: The receipts arose from the taxpayer’s activity of developing and subletting property as a trading operation.
predicates.residuary_income_category_not_applied: The receipts are not assigned to a residual income category when they fall within a specific category.

issues.definition: When an income-tax classification case concerns receipts arising from a trading operation, the residual category is not applied to those receipts.

issues.legal_issue: Assessment of income under the property-income category requires that the taxpayer own the buildings or appurtenant land.
material_facts: The company took the market premises on lease and sublet portions of them.
There was no finding that the company owned the property or any part of it.
The parties agreed that assessment of the company under the property-income category did not arise on these facts.
issues.conclusion: The property-income category in section 9 of the Income-tax Act, 1922, did not apply because the company was not found to be the owner of the property.
issues.legal_principle: Section 9 of the Income-tax Act, 1922, imposes liability under the property-income head on the owner of buildings or appurtenant land. The Court referred to East India Housing and Land Development Trust Ltd. v. Commissioner of Income-tax for the rule concerning income derived by an owner.

predicates.income_tax_classification_case: The dispute concerns how receipts are to be classified for income-tax assessment.
predicates.taxpayer_is_not_property_owner: The taxpayer held the property as a lessee, and there was no finding that it owned the property.
predicates.property_income_category_not_applied: The receipts are not assessed as income derived by the taxpayer from property it owns.

issues.definition: When an income-tax classification case concerns a taxpayer who is not the property owner, the receipts are not assigned to the owner-based property-income category.
